rows.subtype: Approach: overnight resolution to change everything [Pitfall]
rows.description: After a bad exam, the student resolves to sleep at 9 pm and wake at 4 am starting tomorrow. The unrealistic jump fails in two days and leaves the student feeling like a failure.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: emotion-aware planning, forward planning, if-then plan

rows.subtype: Approach: wind-down routine with if-then rules [Thinking]
rows.description: The student decides that if it is 10 pm then the phone charges outside the room, and a short routine of washing up and reading follows, giving the brain a repeated signal for sleep.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: emotion-aware planning, forward planning, sleeping on it

rows.subtype: Approach: relying on caffeine and energy drinks [Pitfall]
rows.description: To stay alert, the student drinks strong tea and energy drinks late in the day. It masks tiredness briefly but delays sleep, so the next day starts even more drained.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: emotion-aware planning, forward planning, if-then plan, sleeping on it

rows.subtype: Approach: tracking sleep and mood in a diary [Action]
rows.description: For two weeks the student notes bedtime, wake time and how focused the next day felt, and sees that focus is clearly best after seven to eight hours, a personal proof that motivates change.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: forward planning, if-then plan, sleeping on it

rows.description: The student sets a fixed wake time, opens curtains for daylight, does light exercise and has breakfast, since a strong morning routine helps the body clock more than forcing an early bedtime.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: emotion-aware planning, if-then plan, sleeping on it

rows.subtype: Approach: involving family in the routine [Action]
rows.description: The student asks parents to switch off the living-room TV at 10 pm and keep the home quiet, showing that changes are easier when the household environment supports them.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: emotion-aware planning, if-then plan, sleeping on it

rows.subtype: Approach: relapse after a festival or exam week and restarting [Revision]
rows.description: After a week of late nights around a wedding, the student does not give up but simply returns to the fixed wake time the next morning, treating the slip as normal rather than proof of failure.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: emotion-aware planning, forward planning, if-then plan

rows.subtype: Approach: seeking a doctor when routine change is not enough [Revision]
rows.description: When months of good habits still leave the student sleepless and exhausted, the family consults a doctor, treating persistent sleep trouble as something professionals should assess.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: emotion-aware planning, if-then plan, sleeping on it

rows.description: After a low result, the student allows a day of disappointment, talks to a friend and avoids big decisions, knowing that plans made in shock, such as quitting school, are often regretted.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, lateral thinking, learning from past failure, seeking advice

rows.subtype: Approach: analysing what happened with the answer sheet [Action]
rows.description: The student requests the paper review, sorts lost marks into knowledge gaps, time management and carelessness, and finds that poor time management in the last section caused most of the loss.
